examples.ja: 家を買うために、毎月貯金している。
examples.en: I'm saving money every month in order to buy a house.

examples.ja: 大雪のために、電車が止まった。
examples.en: The trains stopped because of the heavy snow.

fill.q: 留学する（　）、アルバイトをしてお金をためている。
fill.why: 留学する is volitional with the same subject, so purpose is 〜ために.
fill.en: I'm working part-time and saving money in order to study abroad.

wrong.ように: 〜ように marks a goal with non-volitional verbs; 留学する is volitional by the same subject, so ために fits.
wrong.せいで: 〜せいで means 'because of (a bad result)'; it doesn't express a goal.
wrong.ことに: 〜ことにする/なる means 'decide / it's decided'; it needs する or なる after it.

fill.q: 事故の（　）、道がとても込んでいる。
fill.why: N + のために as a neutral cause.
fill.en: Because of an accident, the road is very crowded.

wrong.ように: 〜ように means 'so that / like'; 事故のように would mean 'like an accident', not a cause.
wrong.おかげで: 〜おかげで means 'thanks to' for good results; a crowded road is a bad result.
wrong.とおりに: 〜とおりに means 'as / according to'; 'as the accident, crowded' makes no sense.

fill.q: 健康の（　）、毎朝ジョギングをしています。
fill.why: N + のために = for the sake of.
fill.en: I go jogging every morning for my health.

wrong.ように: 〜ように after a noun means 'like'; 健康のように would mean 'like health', not 'for health'.
wrong.せいで: 〜せいで means 'because of (bad result)'; jogging isn't a bad result of health.
wrong.くせに: 〜くせに means 'even though' with criticism; it doesn't express a purpose.

order.en: I'm studying every day in order to get into a Japanese university.

formation: N + によって + V / N + による + N
note: Shows variation (人によって違う), the agent in passive sentences about creation, or a cause. Use による before a noun. Compare 〜について (about) and 〜によると (according to).

examples.ja: 考え方は人によって違う。
examples.en: Ways of thinking differ from person to person.

examples.ja: 大雨によって、川の水が増えた。
examples.en: The river rose because of the heavy rain.

fill.q: 国（　）、文化や習慣が違う。
fill.why: Variation: 'differs depending on the country'.
fill.en: Culture and customs differ from country to country.

wrong.について: 〜について means 'about'; 'about countries, culture differs' doesn't mean 'depending on the country'.
wrong.にとって: 〜にとって means 'for / from the viewpoint of'; it doesn't express variation by country.
wrong.に対して: 〜に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it doesn't mean 'differ depending on'.

fill.q: 大雨（　）事故で、道路が通れなくなった。
fill.why: Cause before a noun: 〜による + N.
fill.en: Because of an accident caused by heavy rain, the road became impassable.

wrong.について: 〜についての means 'about'; before a noun it needs の, and 'an accident about heavy rain' makes no sense.
wrong.にとって: 〜にとって means 'for (someone)'; it doesn't express a cause.
wrong.に対する: 〜に対する means 'toward / against'; 'an accident toward heavy rain' makes no sense.

fill.q: この小説は、有名な作家（　）書かれた。
fill.why: The agent of a passive creation verb: 〜によって.
fill.en: This novel was written by a famous author.

wrong.にとって: 〜にとって means 'for (someone)'; it can't mark the agent of a passive verb.
wrong.について: 〜について means 'about'; 'written about a famous author' changes the meaning—the author didn't write it.
wrong.に対して: 〜に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it can't mark who wrote the book.

formation: N + によると（によれば）
note: Gives the source of information; the sentence usually ends with 〜そうだ or 〜らしい. Compare 〜によって (depending on / by).

examples.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れるそうだ。
examples.en: According to the weather forecast, it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: 新聞によると、この町の人口が増えているらしい。
examples.en: According to the newspaper, this town's population is growing.

fill.q: ニュース（　）、来月から電気代が上がるそうだ。
fill.why: The source of information is marked by 〜によると.
fill.en: According to the news, electricity bills will go up from next month.

wrong.によって: 〜によって means 'depending on / by means of'; for an information source before そうだ, use によると.
wrong.について: 〜について means 'about'; 'about the news, bills will rise' doesn't mark the source.
wrong.にとって: 〜にとって means 'for (someone)'; it can't mark where information came from.

fill.q: 母の話（　）、兄は来年結婚するらしい。
fill.why: 〜の話によると = according to what someone said.
fill.en: According to my mother, my older brother is apparently getting married next year.

wrong.にとって: 〜にとって means 'for (someone)'; it can't mark the source of information.
wrong.に対して: 〜に対して means 'toward / in contrast to'; it doesn't mark where you heard something.
wrong.として: 〜として means 'as (a role)'; 'as my mother's story' doesn't fit.

fill.q: 天気予報によると、明日は雨が（　）。
fill.why: 〜によると pairs with hearsay 〜そうだ (plain form).
fill.en: According to the weather forecast, it's supposed to rain tomorrow.

wrong.降るようにする: 〜ようにする means 'make an effort to / make sure that'; rain isn't something anyone does on purpose, and it doesn't report a forecast.
wrong.降ろう: The volitional form means 'let's / I'll' and expresses someone's intention; rain has no will, and it doesn't report hearsay.
wrong.降るつもりだ: 〜つもりだ means 'intend to' and describes a person's plan; rain can't intend anything, and after によると you need hearsay そうだ.

formation: N + について / N + についての + N
note: Marks the topic being discussed, studied or thought about. Use についての before a noun. Compare 〜に対して (toward a person or thing).

examples.ja: 日本の歴史について調べています。
examples.en: I'm researching Japanese history.

examples.ja: 環境問題についてどう思いますか。
examples.en: What do you think about environmental problems?

fill.q: 明日の会議（　）、何か質問はありますか。
fill.why: The topic of questions: 〜について.
fill.en: Are there any questions about tomorrow's meeting?

wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of' someone; a meeting has no point of view, and you want 'questions about' it.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on / due to'; 'questions depending on the meeting' doesn't make sense here.
wrong.として: Means 'as (a role)'; the meeting isn't a role or category, you need 'about' the meeting.

fill.q: レポートは日本の食文化（　）書くつもりだ。
fill.why: The topic of writing: 〜について.
fill.en: I plan to write my report about Japanese food culture.

wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of' someone; food culture can't have a viewpoint, and 書く needs a topic: 'about'.
wrong.によると: Means 'according to' a source of information and leads to hearsay; you write about a topic, not according to it.
wrong.に比べて: Means 'compared with'; it would need a comparison like 'more ... than', but here food culture is simply the topic.

fill.q: この町の歴史（　）本を読んだ。
fill.why: Before a noun, use 〜についての.
fill.en: I read a book about the history of this town.

wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of' someone; history can't have a viewpoint, and before 本 you need a noun-modifying 'about'.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on / due to'; 'a book by the town's history' makes no sense, and て-form can't directly modify 本.
wrong.として: Means 'as (a role)'; the history isn't a role, and a noun like 本 needs a modifier form such as についての.

formation: N + に対して / N + に対する + N / plain (な-adj + な) + のに対して
note: Marks the target of an action or attitude, or contrasts two things (〜のに対して). Compare 〜について (topic) and 〜にとって (from someone's viewpoint).

examples.ja: 先生は学生に対してとても厳しい。
examples.en: The teacher is very strict with the students.

examples.ja: 兄は背が高いのに対して、弟は低い。
examples.en: My older brother is tall, whereas my younger brother is short.

fill.q: 客（　）失礼なことを言ってはいけない。
fill.why: The target of rude words: 〜に対して.
fill.en: You must not say rude things to customers.

wrong.について: Means 'about (a topic)'; 'say rude things about customers' changes the meaning, the point is saying them toward customers.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on / due to'; 'rude things depending on the customer' isn't the meaning, you need 'toward'.
wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of'; it goes with evaluations (difficult, important), not with an action aimed at someone.

fill.q: 姉は明るい性格なの（　）、妹はおとなしい。
fill.why: Contrast between two people: 〜のに対して.
fill.en: My older sister is cheerful, whereas my younger sister is quiet.

wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of' someone; it doesn't contrast two things, and it attaches to nouns, not なの.
wrong.について: Means 'about (a topic)'; it can't link two clauses to show a contrast like 'whereas'.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on / due to'; it doesn't express the contrast 'whereas' between the two sisters.

fill.q: 私の質問（　）、彼は何も答えなかった。
fill.why: The thing being responded to: 〜に対して.
fill.en: He didn't answer my question at all.

wrong.にとって: Means 'for / from the viewpoint of' someone; a question has no viewpoint, and 答える needs a target: 'to my question'.
wrong.として: Means 'as (a role)'; my question isn't a role he played, you need the target of his response.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on / due to'; 'he didn't answer depending on my question' doesn't fit, you need 'to/in response to'.

formation: N + にとって（は／も）
note: Gives the viewpoint from which something is judged, usually followed by an evaluation (大切, 難しい). Compare 〜に対して (an action toward someone).

examples.ja: 私にとって、家族が一番大切です。
examples.en: For me, family is the most important thing.

examples.ja: この問題は子どもにとって難しすぎる。
examples.en: This problem is too difficult for children.

fill.q: 学生（　）、夏休みは一番楽しい時期だ。
fill.why: The viewpoint for an evaluation: 〜にとって.
fill.en: For students, summer vacation is the most fun time.

wrong.に対して: Means 'toward / against' (an action aimed at someone); here you're giving an evaluation from students' viewpoint, so にとって.
wrong.について: Means 'about (a topic)'; the sentence evaluates summer from students' standpoint rather than talking about students.
wrong.によって: Means 'by / depending on'; 'depending on the student' would be a different idea from 'for students, it's the best time'.

fill.q: この写真は、私（　）大切な思い出だ。
fill.why: 'Precious to me' is 〜にとって大切.
fill.en: This photo is a precious memory for me.

wrong.について: Means 'about (a topic)'; 'a precious memory about me' isn't the idea, it's precious from my point of view.
wrong.に対して: Means 'toward / against' and needs an action aimed at someone; 大切な思い出だ is an evaluation, which takes にとって.
wrong.として: Means 'as (a role)'; 'precious memory as me' makes no sense, you need 'for me'.

fill.q: 外国人（　）、日本語のけいごは難しい。
fill.why: Difficulty judged from someone's viewpoint: 〜にとって.
fill.en: For foreigners, Japanese honorific language is difficult.

wrong.に対して: Means 'toward / against' an action's target; 'difficult' is a judgment from someone's standpoint, which takes にとって.
wrong.について: Means 'about (a topic)'; keigo isn't difficult 'about foreigners', it's difficult for them.
wrong.によると: Means 'according to' a source of information; it would need hearsay like そうだ, and foreigners aren't the source here.

formation: N + として（は／も／の + N）
note: Shows the role, position or category in which someone or something acts or is seen. Compare 〜にとって (from someone's viewpoint).

examples.ja: 彼は通訳として会議に参加した。

examples.ja: 京都は古い町として有名だ。

wrong.として: Means 'as (a role)'; 'sang as my friends' makes no sense, you need 'together with'.

wrong.って: 使わって isn't a valid form; the te-form is 使って, and permission needs 使わせて.

meaning: when I did ~, (I found / it turned out) ~
formation: V-たら + past result (discovery or unexpected event)
note: The second part is something the speaker discovered or that happened unexpectedly, not under their control. Similar to 〜と〜た, but more conversational.

examples.ja: 家に帰ったら、母が来ていた。
examples.en: When I got home, my mother was there.

examples.ja: 窓を開けたら、雪が降っていた。
examples.en: When I opened the window, it was snowing.

fill.q: 冷蔵庫を開け（　）、ケーキがなくなっていた。
fill.why: 〜たら〜た: when I opened it, I found...
fill.en: When I opened the fridge, the cake was gone.

wrong.ても: 〜ても means 'even if'; 'even if I opened it, the cake was gone' doesn't fit a discovery.
wrong.ながら: 〜ながら means 'while doing'; it doesn't express discovering something on opening.
wrong.ずに: 〜ずに means 'without doing'; you can't find the cake gone without opening the fridge.

fill.q: 駅に着いたら、電車はもう出て（　）。
fill.why: What you found on arriving is a past state: 出ていた (had already left).
fill.en: When I got to the station, the train had already left.

wrong.いる: 〜たら〜た describes a past discovery, so the ending must be past (出ていた).
wrong.いく: 〜ていく means 'go away / continue'; with たら〜た the ending must be past tense.
wrong.おく: 〜ておく means 'do in advance'; it doesn't describe what you found and isn't past.

fill.q: 薬を飲んだら、すぐに熱が（　）。
fill.why: 〜たら〜た: the result that followed (the fever went down) is a past fact.
fill.en: When I took the medicine, my fever went down right away.

wrong.下がろう: 〜よう is volitional ('let's'); a fever can't intend anything, and the result needs past.
wrong.下がりたい: 〜たい means 'want to'; it doesn't describe what actually happened.
wrong.下げよう: 下げる is transitive and よう is volitional; the result after たら should be 下がった.
